text:
alex: Hey team — opened a small TF refactor PR to dedupe provider blocks and move provider configs to the repo root. Also switching to a single providers lockfile. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4287 Can someone quick-check the GKE secrets wiring and any provider alias fallout?

priya: skimmed the diff. main concern: Vault path rename from `k8s/ci/sa-key` -> `k8s/service-accounts/ci/key.json`. Consumers that reference the old path will break unless ops adds an alias. Also hoisting providers means modules must use `providers = { google = google }` instead of declaring their own.

matt: noted — we also have a few modules still relying on `google-beta` alias. PR looks like it replaced inline provider blocks with forwarded provider mappings in module calls. Need to ensure aliases are preserved for the beta API where required.

sam: fwiw I ran `terraform init -upgrade` + `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` locally and regenerated the lockfile. Plan shows no resource diffs except provider addresses. Snippet from PR for clarity:
```hcl
# before: each module had its own provider block
provider "google" {
  project = var.project
}

# after: single provider in root, modules receive it
provider "google" {
  project = var.project
}
module "gke" {
  source = "./modules/gke"
  providers = { google = google }
}
```

lia: small ops note: k8s manifests reference `secretKeyRef: name: ci-key` and the Kubernetes secret name will not change; only the Vault path backing that secret is being moved. Make sure Vault alias is created so automated sync still finds the secret.

terraform-bot: Heads up — CI will reject the PR if the lockfile in the branch doesn't match the checked-in `terraform.lock.hcl`. The CI job `tools/ci/terraform-lock-check` will fail and post details in the PR.

alex: thanks. @sam can you add a short migration section in the PR description with the exact commands to regenerate the lockfile and local smoke steps? @priya can you coordinate with ops to add the Vault alias?

sam: done — added checklist to PR:
- run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64`
- run `make tf-smoke` against staging
- run `make tf-plan -target=module.gke` and verify no resource replacements
I also left a comment reminding reviewers to watch for `google-beta` alias usage.

priya: I'll ping ops now and paste the alias request. If they confirm, I'm fine with merging after CI is green. :thumbsup:

matt: +1 from me. Post-merge we should run the staging plan and hold off on apply until we confirm no drift.

alex: awesome — plan: wait for ops + CI. If both OK, merge and coordinate a short maintenance window for the first apply. Thanks everyone :pray:
